sentences.zh: 在美伊之间这场持续了近四个月的冲突中，我们正处于这样一个时刻：双方的敌意和不信任

sentences.zh: 而那些本应建立在这种脆弱的后现代停火基础上的和平谈判，也几乎是一团糟。

sentences.en: And at the heart of this all is a profound decades-old hatred, and I don't think that's too strong a word, between the governments of Iran and the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这一切的核心是一种深层的、持续了几十年的仇恨——我觉得用这个词并不为过——存在于伊朗和美国政府之间。

sentences.en: And it's a hatred whose origins we've never quite definitively told the story of on this show.
sentences.zh: 这种仇恨的起源，我们在这个节目中从未完整地讲述过。

sentences.en: And you, not long before the war began, told that story in what turned out to be a very well-timed book called King of Kings.
sentences.zh: 而在战争开始前不久，你在一本名为《万王之王》的书中讲述了这个故事，那本书出版的时机非常巧妙。

sentences.en: And what your book so powerfully recounts is that this relationship between the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你的书有力地重现了这样一个事实：美伊之间的这种关系，

sentences.en: and Iran wasn't always filled with animus.
sentences.zh: 并非一直充满敌意。

sentences.zh: 恰恰相反，在过去50年里，美国

sentences.en: relationship with Iran went from a deeply intertwined alliance that was respectful and at times even affectionate to this much darker thing that we now know today.
sentences.zh: 与伊朗的关系从一种相互尊重、有时甚至充满温情的紧密联盟，变成了我们今天所知的这种更加黑暗的状态。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: If you go back exactly 50 years ago today,
sentences.zh: 如果你回到整整50年前的今天，

sentences.en: Iran was America's most important ally between Western Europe and Japan.
sentences.zh: 伊朗是美国在西欧和日本之间最重要的盟友。

sentences.en: The two economies were inextricably linked.
sentences.zh: 两国的经济紧密相连，不可分割。

sentences.en: Economically, of course, we were getting Iranian oil.
sentences.zh: 在经济上，我们当然是在获取伊朗的石油。

sentences.en: Iran was the biggest, by far, the biggest buyer of American arms abroad.
sentences.zh: 伊朗是美国海外武器最大的买家，遥遥领先。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Planes, missiles, bombs.

sentences.en: Everything.
sentences.zh: 应有尽有。

sentences.en: Everything short of nuclear weapons.
sentences.zh: 除了核武器，什么都卖。

sentences.en: Kind of a staggering thing to contemplate today.
sentences.zh: 这在今天看来简直令人震惊。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: 50,000 Americans were living in Iran, and 50,000 Iranian students were studying at American universities.
sentences.zh: 当时有5万名美国人生活在伊朗，也有5万名伊朗学生在美国的大学里学习。

sentences.en: The Shah had visited the United States a dozen times over his reign.
sentences.zh: 国王在位期间曾十几次访问美国。

sentences.en: He'd met seven different presidents at the White House, and American presidents had come to Tehran to meet with him.
sentences.zh: 他在白宫见过七位不同的美国总统，美国总统也曾到德黑兰与他会面。

sentences.en: It's like an alternate universe.
sentences.zh: 这就像另一个宇宙。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They were incredibly close.
sentences.zh: 他们曾经极其亲密。

sentences.en: And what is ironic in a story full of ironies is that the very closeness of that relationship
sentences.zh: 在一个充满讽刺的故事中，最讽刺的是，美伊之间这种关系的亲密程度，

sentences.en: between the Americans and the Iranians carried the seeds of the revolution that was to come.
sentences.zh: 反而埋下了后来革命的种子。

sentences.en: And Scott, in your book, you explain that historians still marvel at the improbability of the revolution
sentences.zh: 斯科特，你在书中解释说，历史学家至今仍对那场革命的不可思议感到惊叹，

sentences.en: that you just referred to, this total inferno of a rejection of the West in a country so thoroughly dominated by a partnership with the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 也就是你刚才提到的，在一个与西方有着如此深厚伙伴关系的国家里，竟然爆发了如此彻底的、对西方的排斥狂潮。

sentences.en: No, that's right.
sentences.zh: 不，你说得对。

sentences.en: And how this all just unraveled over the course of a year is just astonishing.
sentences.zh: 这一切在一年之内如何土崩瓦解，简直令人震惊。

sentences.en: And in looking at the dynamics of the revolution, there seem so many moments when if something had played out just slightly different,
sentences.zh: 回顾革命的动态，似乎有许多时刻，如果事情的发展稍有不同，

sentences.en: if someone had made a decision or not made a decision, that it all could have played out very, very differently, or been aborted altogether.
sentences.zh: 如果有人做出了不同的决定，或者没有做出某个决定，一切都可能走向完全不同的结局，甚至可能完全被阻止。

sentences.en: You know, it wasn't like going into a house and opening the wrong door.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这不像走进一间屋子却开错了门。

sentences.en: It was like going into a house and opening 43 wrong doors in a row.
sentences.zh: 这就像走进一间屋子，连续开了43扇错误的门。

sentences.en: That's what happened here.
sentences.zh: 这就是当时发生的情况。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, let's begin our effort to understand how so many wrong doors were opened by first really making sense of how it ever was the case
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们开始尝试理解为什么会开了这么多错误的门，首先要弄清楚的是，

sentences.en: that the United States and Iran became such full intertwined partners.
sentences.zh: 美国和伊朗究竟是如何成为如此紧密的伙伴的。

sentences.en: Because as we're making very clear here, that doesn't make much sense given where we are today.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们刚才明确指出的，考虑到今天的现状，这似乎不太合逻辑。

sentences.en: But it obviously made all the sense in the world while it was actually happening.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，这显然是再合理不过的事情了。

sentences.en: So what is the story of how these two countries and militaries, governments, and economies became so interwoven?
sentences.zh: 那么，这两个国家的军队、政府和经济是如何变得如此交织在一起的呢？

sentences.en: So in order to understand this entire story of the U.S.-Iran relationship and how the two countries got so close,
sentences.zh: 为了理解美伊关系的整个故事，以及两国是如何变得如此亲密的，

sentences.en: you need to understand who the leader of Iran was for a very long stretch of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 你需要了解20世纪很长一段时间里伊朗的领导人是谁。

sentences.en: His name was Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, and he was known as the Shah, which is Persian for king.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫穆罕默德·礼萨·巴列维，被称为“沙阿”，在波斯语中意为“国王”。

sentences.en: The Shah came to power in 1941 after the British and Soviets overthrew his father, who had been the former Shah.
sentences.zh: 1941年，在英国和苏联推翻了前任国王（他的父亲）后，沙阿上台了。

sentences.en: And they put the young Shah, he was 21, on the throne because they saw him as weak and ineffectual.
sentences.zh: 他们把年仅21岁的年轻沙阿扶上王位，因为他们认为他软弱无能。

sentences.en: But the Shah's trajectory really starts to change once his relationship with the United States started to blossom.
sentences.zh: 但沙阿的人生轨迹在与美国的关系开始升温后，真正发生了改变。

sentences.en: And a key moment of that was in 1953.
sentences.zh: 其中一个关键时刻是在1953年。

sentences.en: There was a parliamentary crisis in Iran.
sentences.zh: 当时伊朗发生了议会危机。

sentences.en: There was a new prime minister named Mohammad Mossadegh.
sentences.zh: 出现了一位名叫穆罕默德·摩萨台的新首相。

sentences.en: He was a populist and a bit of a firebrand, very charismatic.
sentences.zh: 他是一位民粹主义者，有点煽动性，非常有魅力。

sentences.en: And he was kind of the first time there was a prime minister who really started to assert against the Shah.
sentences.zh: 他算是第一位真正开始挑战沙阿权威的首相。

sentences.en: Not just to assert, but to start to strip the Shah of his powers.
sentences.zh: 不仅是挑战，还开始剥夺沙阿的权力。

sentences.en: And one issue that really galvanized his authority and his popularity in the country was his move to nationalize Iran's oil industry.
sentences.zh: 而一个真正激发他在国内权威和人气的议题，是他推动了伊朗石油工业的国有化。

sentences.en: Take it over.
sentences.zh: 接管它。

sentences.en: From who?
sentences.zh: 从谁手里？

sentences.en: Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 英国。

sentences.en: Since the beginning of the century, the British government controlled Iran's oil industry, paying the Iranian government a pittance.
sentences.zh: 自本世纪初以来，英国政府一直控制着伊朗的石油工业，只付给伊朗政府微薄的报酬。

sentences.en: So when Mossadegh came to power, this was the primary issue that he was using to galvanize his support and also to move against the Shah.
sentences.zh: 所以当摩萨台掌权时，这是他用来凝聚支持并对抗沙阿的主要议题。

sentences.en: And what did the Shah think should be happening to Iran's oil?
sentences.zh: 那么沙阿认为伊朗的石油应该怎么办？

sentences.en: Should it be nationalized?
sentences.zh: 应该国有化吗？

sentences.en: The Shah was much more cautious.
sentences.zh: 沙阿要谨慎得多。

sentences.en: In public, he would talk about that he was in support of nationalization, but that it should be taken gradually and moderately and responsibly.
sentences.zh: 在公开场合，他会说他支持国有化，但应该循序渐进、温和且负责任地进行。

sentences.en: But behind the scenes, he was telling the British, I'm your guy.
sentences.zh: 但在幕后，他却在告诉英国人：“我是你们的人。”

sentences.en: So it set up this constitutional crisis between these two men.
sentences.zh: 于是，这两人之间引发了一场宪政危机。

sentences.en: And it became a question of who is really in charge.
sentences.zh: 问题变成了谁才是真正的掌权者。

sentences.en: Is it the Shah or is it Prime Minister Mossadegh?
sentences.zh: 是沙阿，还是摩萨台首相？

sentences.en: And so the British, fearing they were going to lose their oil monopoly, they come up with this idea that, well,
sentences.zh: 于是，担心失去石油垄断权的英国人想出了一个主意，那就是：

sentences.en: we'll overthrow Mossadegh and restore the Shah to his full kingly powers.
sentences.zh: 我们推翻摩萨台，恢复沙阿的全部王权。

sentences.en: But the British were very smart about this.
sentences.zh: 但英国人在这一点上非常聪明。

sentences.en: They didn't want to have their own hands be shown in the coup.
sentences.zh: 他们不想让自己的手出现在政变中。

sentences.en: So they got the United States to do it for them.
sentences.zh: 所以他们让美国人代劳。

sentences.en: They told the Eisenhower administration, Mossadegh is soft on communism.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉艾森豪威尔政府：“摩萨台对共产主义态度软弱。”

sentences.en: The communists are just waiting in the wings to take over in Iran.
sentences.zh: “共产党人正伺机在伊朗夺权。”

sentences.en: That actually wasn't true at all.
sentences.zh: 这其实根本不是事实。

sentences.en: Mossadegh was an anti-communiSt.
sentences.zh: 摩萨台是反共的。

sentences.en: But of course, this is a time in the Cold War when Americans are terrified of the spread of communism around the world.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这是冷战时期，美国人对共产主义在全球的蔓延感到恐惧。

sentences.en: So the Eisenhower administration says, all right, we'll take care of this problem for you.
sentences.zh: 所以艾森豪威尔政府说：“好吧，我们会帮你解决这个问题。”

sentences.en: We'll get rid of Mossadegh and restore the Shah to his power.
sentences.zh: “我们会除掉摩萨台，恢复沙阿的权力。”

sentences.en: We'll take on the coup.
sentences.zh: “我们来发动这场政变。”

sentences.en: The British understood the American Cold War mentality, which is if we have to do a coup in order to stop communism, we'll do the coup.
sentences.zh: 英国人了解美国人的冷战心态，即：如果我们必须通过政变来阻止共产主义，那我们就发动政变。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It plays right into the American Cold War mentalities.
sentences.zh: 这完全迎合了美国的冷战心态。

sentences.en: So in the summer of 1953, the CIA essentially stirred this coup against Mossadegh.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1953年夏天，中央情报局本质上策划了这场针对摩萨台的政变。

sentences.en: The Shah demanded Mossadegh's resignation.
sentences.zh: 沙阿要求摩萨台辞职。

sentences.en: The premier refused and fresh rioting broke out in the capital city of Tehran.
sentences.zh: 首相拒绝了，首都德黑兰爆发了新的骚乱。

sentences.en: So this coup goes awry almost immediately and it takes place over a very complicated and chaotic four days in Tehran, where it appears one side is winning and then the other.
sentences.zh: 这场政变几乎立即陷入混乱，在德黑兰经历了复杂且混乱的四天，期间看起来似乎是一方获胜，然后又是另一方。

sentences.en: In a brazen act of defiance, the statue of the Shah's father is toppled from its pedestal.
sentences.zh: 在一次大胆的挑衅行为中，沙阿父亲的雕像被从基座上推倒了。

sentences.en: The Shah leaves.
sentences.zh: 沙阿离开了。

sentences.en: The Shah leaves Iran.
sentences.zh: 沙阿离开了伊朗。

sentences.en: Fearing for his life, the Shah's advisors advocated his temporary exile to Rome.
sentences.zh: 出于对自身安全的担忧，沙阿的顾问建议他暂时流亡到罗马。

sentences.en: When he finds out that the coup has been a success on his part, he's having lunch at the Excelsior Hotel in Rome.
sentences.zh: 当他得知政变在他这一方取得成功时，他正在罗马的埃克塞尔西奥酒店吃午餐。

sentences.en: In the quick shift of power, Mossadegh was finally apprehended and awaits trial for treason.
sentences.zh: 在权力的快速更迭中，摩萨台最终被捕，等待叛国罪的审判。

sentences.en: The Shah who had fled to Rome comes home.
sentences.zh: 逃往罗马的沙阿回国了。

sentences.en: And he comes back, you know, a little bit tail between his legs two or three days later to assume the throne.
sentences.zh: 两三天后，他灰溜溜地回来了，重新登上了王位。

sentences.en: Now crowds shout pro-Shah slogans and carry pictures of the troubled ruler of a troubled nation.
sentences.zh: 现在，人群高呼支持沙阿的口号，举着这位陷入困境的国家领导人的照片。

sentences.en: So, in a sense, he flees his own coup.
sentences.zh: 所以，从某种意义上说，他是逃离了自己的政变。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Comes back, discovers he's now in power thanks to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 回来后发现，多亏了美国，他现在掌权了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What is important about the 53 coup is from that moment on, every Iranian knows about the coup and they know about the American role in it.
sentences.zh: 关于53年政变，重要的一点是，从那一刻起，每个伊朗人都知道这场政变，也知道美国在其中扮演的角色。

sentences.en: The Shah becomes, quote, the American Shah.
sentences.zh: 沙阿成了所谓的“美国沙阿”。

sentences.en: Even in the eyes of his supporters, he is seen as joined to the hip to the Americans.
sentences.zh: 即使在他的支持者眼中，他也与美国人绑在了一起。

sentences.en: Because he owes his power to the Americans.
sentences.zh: 因为他的权力归功于美国人。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If you're Iranian, Scott, this phrase, American Shah, is that a good thing or a bad thing at this moment in history?
sentences.zh: 斯科特，如果你是伊朗人，“美国沙阿”这个词在当时的历史时刻是好事还是坏事？

sentences.en: It's a combination of good and bad.
sentences.zh: 这是好坏参半的。

sentences.en: I think you get to this very complicated national personality of Iran, of Iranians, where for centuries they've wanted to emulate the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为这触及了伊朗人非常复杂的民族性格，几个世纪以来，他们一直想效仿西方。

sentences.en: They're bitter of how they've been mistreated and taken advantage of.
sentences.zh: 他们对被虐待和被利用感到痛苦。

sentences.en: So, it's kind of this complicated love-hate relationship.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种复杂的爱恨交织的关系。

sentences.en: Emulation and then resentment.
sentences.zh: 效仿，然后是怨恨。

sentences.en: Resentment, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，怨恨。

sentences.en: And it runs very, very deep.
sentences.zh: 而且这种怨恨根深蒂固。

sentences.en: But from the Shah's point of view, this relationship with the United States feels like a golden opportunity.
sentences.zh: 但从沙阿的角度来看，这种与美国的关系感觉是一个千载难逢的机会。

sentences.en: For centuries, Iran had been a kind of pawn on the global stage, yanked back and forth among the great empires of Britain and Russia.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，伊朗一直是全球舞台上的一枚棋子，在英国和俄罗斯等大帝国之间被拉来扯去。

sentences.en: And the Shah was looking for an outside ally, what he called a third force,
sentences.zh: 沙阿一直在寻找一个外部盟友，他称之为“第三势力”，

sentences.en: some power strong enough to defend Iran and liberate the country from this long period of being exploited by these external great powers.
sentences.zh: 一种足够强大的力量来保卫伊朗，并将国家从长期被这些外部大国剥削的境地中解放出来。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And he sees the United States as potentially that third force ally.
sentences.zh: 他将美国视为潜在的第三股盟友力量。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But actually, the Americans really don't see any advantage at this moment to having a long-term relationship with the Shah or with Iran.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，美国人目前并不觉得与沙阿或伊朗建立长期关系有什么好处。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: They're not interested in opening yet another front in the Middle East in the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 他们对在冷战时期的中东开辟另一个战场并不感兴趣。

sentences.en: And they had no need for Iran's oil.
sentences.zh: 而且他们根本不需要伊朗的石油。

sentences.en: At that time, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当时，美国

sentences.en: had plenty of oil of its own.
sentences.zh: 自己就有充足的石油。

sentences.en: So, this just wasn't a compelling partnership to them.
sentences.zh: 所以，这对他们来说并不是一个有吸引力的伙伴关系。

sentences.en: And if anything, they looked even more askance at the Shah in the wake of the 1953 coup, because who runs away from their own coup?
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么不同的话，那就是在1953年政变后，他们对沙阿更加不屑一顾了，因为有谁会从自己的政变中逃跑呢？

sentences.en: Doesn't make him seem super sturdy as an ally.
sentences.zh: 这让他看起来不像是一个非常可靠的盟友。

sentences.en: So, how did that relationship start to change?
sentences.zh: 那么，这种关系是如何开始改变的呢？

sentences.en: It's a slow build, and it goes much slower than the Shah would wish.
sentences.zh: 这是一个缓慢的过程，而且比沙阿所希望的要慢得多。

sentences.en: The Americans were kind of keeping him at arm's length, really, through the rest of the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 整个20世纪50年代，美国人其实一直对他保持着某种距离。

sentences.en: Even though the Shah, more than almost any other Middle Eastern leader, really embraces Western thinking and Western culture.
sentences.zh: 尽管沙阿比几乎任何其他中东领导人都更拥护西方的思想和文化。

sentences.en: And just explain what you mean by that.
sentences.zh: 请解释一下你这话的意思。

sentences.en: Well, the Shah was a great admirer of Western culture.
sentences.zh: 嗯，沙阿非常崇尚西方文化。

sentences.en: He'd been educated in a Swiss boarding school.
sentences.zh: 他曾在瑞士的寄宿学校接受教育。

sentences.en: He spoke French and English fluently, beautifully.
sentences.zh: 他能说一口流利、优美的法语和英语。

sentences.en: In fact, people at times made fun of his Farsi accent, because they had this idea of him as this internationalist who was out of touch with his own people.
sentences.zh: 事实上，人们有时会取笑他的波斯语口音，因为他们心目中的他是一个与本国人民脱节的国际主义者。

sentences.en: He was very much an internationalist at heart, and quite secular.
sentences.zh: 他内心深处确实是一个国际主义者，而且相当世俗化。

sentences.en: He put on the trappings of being a devout Muslim, but I don't think most people ever really believe that about him.
sentences.zh: 他披上了虔诚穆斯林的外衣，但我认为大多数人从未真正相信这一点。

sentences.en: And he was very comfortable in Europe and European society.
sentences.zh: 他在欧洲和欧洲社会中感到非常自在。

sentences.en: And his instinct was to be Western and make Iran more Western.
sentences.zh: 他的本能是成为西方人，并让伊朗变得更加西方化。

sentences.en: And it's this Western thinking that he begins to bring into Iran in concrete ways that start to really radically change the country and in many ways create the conditions that are going to bring about his own destruction.
sentences.zh: 正是这种西方思想，他开始以具体的方式引入伊朗，这开始从根本上改变这个国家，并在许多方面创造了导致他自身毁灭的条件。

sentences.en: And what do those changes look like?
sentences.zh: 这些变化是什么样的？

sentences.en: You know, this was the early 1960s.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是20世纪60年代初。

sentences.en: And this is a time when there was a lot of social movement for economic progress, for emancipation of women.
sentences.zh: 那是一个为了经济进步、为了妇女解放而进行大量社会运动的时代。

sentences.en: The revolution is the Shah's own blueprint for transforming a backward, feudal society into the grape civilization.
sentences.zh: 这场革命是沙阿自己制定的蓝图，旨在将一个落后的封建社会转变为伟大的文明。

sentences.en: And he wanted Iran to join in that forward movement.
sentences.zh: 他希望伊朗加入那股向前的潮流。

sentences.en: So the Shah institutes this series of 19 social and economic reforms that he calls the White Revolution.
sentences.zh: 于是，沙阿发起了一系列19项社会和经济改革，他称之为“白色革命”。

sentences.en: Part of the Shah's upheaval gave women the vote for the first time.
sentences.zh: 沙阿变革的一部分是首次赋予妇女投票权。

sentences.en: Another was to appoint a woman as minister of education.
sentences.zh: 另一项是任命了一位女性担任教育部长。

sentences.en: And it's everything from reforestation to giving women the right to vote, and really most crucially, agrarian reform.
sentences.zh: 从植树造林到赋予妇女投票权，再到最关键的土地改革，应有尽有。

sentences.en: There is no more a landlord giving orders to, I don't know, scores of peasants.
sentences.zh: 再也没有地主对，我不知道，几十个农民发号施令了。

sentences.en: That is finished.
sentences.zh: 那一切都结束了。

sentences.en: A large majority of the arable land in Iran was under the control of either oligarchic families or the Muslim clergy.
sentences.zh: 伊朗绝大部分可耕地都在寡头家族或穆斯林教士的控制之下。

sentences.en: And so his agrarian reform program was designed to really break up this feudalistic system and finally give landless peasants land.
sentences.zh: 因此，他的土地改革计划旨在真正打破这种封建制度，最终让无地农民拥有土地。

sentences.en: If you are unhappy that your country makes progress, if you are unhappy that your country is saying goodbye to a feudalistic system,
sentences.zh: 如果你对国家取得进步感到不满，如果你对国家告别封建制度感到不满，

sentences.en: if you are unhappy that half of the population of your country, the women, are emancipated, well, this I cannot help.
sentences.zh: 如果你对国家一半的人口——女性——获得解放感到不满，好吧，那我就爱莫能助了。

sentences.en: And all these reforms really enraged the right-wing clergy of the country, which was very, very powerful.
sentences.zh: 所有这些改革确实激怒了该国非常、非常有权势的右翼教士阶层。

sentences.en: And in particular, they enraged an influential cleric named Rukhola Khomeini.
sentences.zh: 特别是，他们激怒了一位名叫鲁霍拉·霍梅尼的有影响力的教士。

sentences.en: Khomeini, far more than almost any other religious opponent to the Shah, was really vituperative in his denunciations of the Shah in the early 1960s.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪60年代初，霍梅尼对沙阿的谴责比几乎任何其他宗教反对者都要尖刻得多。

sentences.en: Called him a false Shah, kind of unheard of.
sentences.zh: 他称他为伪沙阿，这简直闻所未闻。

sentences.en: You would say that in public in Iran.
sentences.zh: 你竟然会在伊朗公开这么说。

sentences.en: He despised the West in general, but especially Israel and the United States.
sentences.zh: 他鄙视整个西方，尤其是以色列和美国。

sentences.en: He saw them as the servants of Satan.
sentences.zh: 他视他们为撒旦的仆人。

sentences.en: And in his writings, he was quite open about that.
sentences.zh: 他在著作中对此毫不掩饰。

sentences.en: So suddenly you have a leading Muslim cleric in the country observing the king of Iran becoming closer and closer to the United States,
sentences.zh: 所以，你突然看到国内一位领先的穆斯林教士观察到伊朗国王与美国的关系越来越近，

sentences.en: instituting political reforms that feel awfully Western and secular.
sentences.zh: 并推行着让人感觉非常西方化和世俗化的政治改革。

sentences.en: And after that 53 coup, owing his very legitimacy to the United States.
sentences.zh: 而且在53年政变后，他的合法性完全归功于美国。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That would seem to be very problematic.
sentences.zh: 这看起来会是非常棘手的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So things with Khomeini reach ahead in 1963.
sentences.zh: 所以，霍梅尼的事情在1963年达到了顶峰。

sentences.en: The Shah moves to arrest Khomeini for some of the incendiary things he's been saying.
sentences.zh: 沙阿采取行动，以霍梅尼发表的一些煽动性言论为由将其逮捕。

sentences.en: Again, the free world is troubled by trouble in Iran.
sentences.zh: 同样，自由世界对伊朗的动荡感到不安。

sentences.en: Khomeini's arrest sets off clerical riots around the country.
sentences.zh: 霍梅尼的被捕引发了全国范围内的教士骚乱。

sentences.en: One of the causes of the new rioting was the Shah's land reform program instituted...
sentences.zh: 新骚乱的原因之一是沙阿推行的土地改革计划……

sentences.en: A number of buildings are burned.
sentences.zh: 许多建筑物被烧毁。

sentences.en: A secondary contributing trouble factor was the Shah's plans for the emancipation of the nation's women.
sentences.zh: 另一个导致动荡的因素是沙阿关于国家妇女解放的计划。

sentences.en: Rioting against this program was led by leaders of a strict Muslim sect opposed to women's suffrage.
sentences.zh: 反对这一计划的骚乱是由反对妇女选举权的严格穆斯林教派领袖领导的。

sentences.en: So the military comes out of their barracks and kills at least 150 people.
sentences.zh: 于是军队从军营中出来，杀死了至少150人。

sentences.en: The opposition said many more than that were killed.
sentences.zh: 反对派称死亡人数远不止于此。

sentences.en: And crucially, Khomeini is arrested.
sentences.zh: 最关键的是，霍梅尼被捕了。

sentences.en: So for the next year, the Shah kept Khomeini in kind of a house arreSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，在接下来的一年里，沙阿将霍梅尼软禁了起来。

sentences.en: The basic deal was, we can coexist as long as you don't make these incendiary public attacks on me.
sentences.zh: 基本的交易是，只要你不对我进行这些煽动性的公开攻击，我们就可以共存。

sentences.en: But Khomeini continued to make those incendiary attacks.
sentences.zh: 但霍梅尼继续进行那些煽动性的攻击。

sentences.en: So less than a year later, the Shah finally re-arrest Khomeini and sends him into exile.
sentences.zh: 所以不到一年后，沙阿最终再次逮捕了霍梅尼并将他流放。

sentences.en: And this is really the moment where the United States finally sits up and takes notice of the Shah.
sentences.zh: 这确实是美国最终开始关注沙阿的时刻。

sentences.en: They think, wow, this guy actually does have a backbone.
sentences.zh: 他们想，哇，这家伙确实有骨气。

sentences.en: He will stand up to his enemies.
sentences.zh: 他会挺身对抗他的敌人。

sentences.en: And he's maybe worth taking seriously.
sentences.zh: 也许他值得认真对待。

sentences.en: And so this is the first moment you really see the United States begin to embrace this partnership that the Shah has been seeking all these years.
sentences.zh: 所以这是你第一次真正看到美国开始拥抱沙阿多年来一直寻求的这种伙伴关系。

sentences.en: So the American Shah finally begins to win over the Americans.
sentences.zh: 所以美国化的沙阿终于开始赢得美国人的青睐了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And on Khomeini's part, he sees the Americans now as the instrument of his exile.
sentences.zh: 而对于霍梅尼来说，他现在将美国人视为他被流放的工具。

sentences.en: And so as anti-American and anti-West as he was before, it's now exponentially more so.
sentences.zh: 所以他以前有多反美、反西方，现在就更是变本加厉了。

sentences.en: But the Shah seems to have learned virtually nothing from Khomeini's uprising of a few years earlier.
sentences.zh: 但沙阿似乎从几年前霍梅尼的起义中几乎什么也没学到。

sentences.en: He doesn't seem to get that his close relationship with the West is any kind of problem.
sentences.zh: 他似乎不明白他与西方的密切关系有什么问题。

sentences.en: And in fact, he does something that just cements how totally enamored he is to the West, even at the expense of regular Iranian people.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他做了一件事，这巩固了他对西方是多么的痴迷，即使是以牺牲普通伊朗人民为代价。

sentences.en: And that happens in October of 1971.
sentences.zh: 那发生在1971年10月。

sentences.en: The Shah wanted to have a grand party to celebrate the 2,500 years of Iranian imperial dynasty at Persepolis, the ancient capital of Persia.
sentences.zh: 沙阿想在波斯古都波斯波利斯举办一场盛大的派对，庆祝伊朗帝国王朝建立2500周年。

sentences.en: There's a three-day extravaganza in the desert where virtually all the guests were foreigners and virtually all the supplies and everything were foreign.
sentences.zh: 沙漠里举行了为期三天的狂欢，几乎所有的客人都是外国人，几乎所有的物资和一切都是外国的。

sentences.en: There will be plenty of food, but the only Iranian dish on the menu is caviar, a few hundred pounds of it.
sentences.zh: 会有充足的食物，但菜单上唯一的伊朗菜是鱼子酱，几百磅的鱼子酱。

sentences.en: All the rest is French.
sentences.zh: 其余的都是法国菜。

sentences.en: Maxime's restaurant in Paris closed down for two weeks and all the waiters of Maxime's came to be the waiters at this banquet.
sentences.zh: 巴黎的马克西姆餐厅关门了两周，马克西姆餐厅所有的服务员都来担任这次宴会的侍者。

sentences.en: No waiters in Iran.
sentences.zh: 伊朗没有服务员。

sentences.en: No waiters.
sentences.zh: 没有服务员。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so it really got to this kind of inferiority complex that the West was the beSt.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的演变成了一种认为西方是最好的自卑情结。

sentences.en: And I have to imagine all these rural religious folks watching their leader put on this extravagant, as you said,
sentences.zh: 我不得不想象，所有这些农村的宗教人士看着他们的领导人举办这场奢华的，正如你所说的，

sentences.en: grotesque banquet on behalf of Western leaders is deeply offensive.
sentences.zh: 代表西方领导人的怪诞宴会，是多么令人深感冒犯。

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是。

sentences.en: Significantly, it was denounced by the exiled Ayatollah Khomeini, who called it the Devil's Festival, and says anyone who attends is participating in murder of the people of Iran.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，它遭到了流亡的阿亚图拉·霍梅尼的谴责，他称之为“魔鬼的节日”，并说任何参加的人都是在参与谋杀伊朗人民。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So I think that at that moment, Khomeini starts seeing this opening of the Shah is really—he's having delusions of grandeur.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在那一刻，霍梅尼开始看到沙阿的这种开放实际上是——他产生了宏大的妄想。

sentences.en: He's losing touch with the reality.
sentences.zh: 他正在失去与现实的联系。

sentences.en: He's losing touch with the reality of most of the Iranian people.
sentences.zh: 他正在失去与大多数伊朗人民现实的联系。

sentences.en: I feel like I'm starting to hear the sound of those many wrong doors you had mentioned earlier starting to open, and it feels like Westernization is central to that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我开始听到你之前提到的那些错误之门开始打开的声音，而且感觉西方化是其中的核心。

sentences.en: So what is happening at this moment with the Shah's relationship to the Americans?
sentences.zh: 那么此时沙阿与美国人的关系发生了什么？

sentences.en: Presumably, it's just getting even closer and closer, right?
sentences.zh: 大概是变得越来越亲密了，对吧？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What's happening is a steady deepening of the relationship.
sentences.zh: 正在发生的是关系的稳步加深。

sentences.en: First, we have military ties between the U.S.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们有美国与伊朗之间的军事联系。

sentences.en: and Iran.
sentences.zh: 美国帮助建立了萨瓦克，即沙阿的秘密警察，它后来因成为沙阿监视民众的工具而臭名昭著，在某些情况下，

sentences.en: The United States helped set up SAVAC, the Shah's secret police, which will become infamous as the Shah's tool to surveil the population, and in some cases,
sentences.zh: 还会拷打异见人士并让人们失踪。

sentences.en: torture dissidents and disappear people.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 美国人在德黑兰建立了一个庞大的中央情报局分站。

sentences.en: The Americans establish a massive CIA station in Tehran.
sentences.zh: 它是中东最大的分站之一，而且还在不断扩大。

sentences.en: It's one of the biggest in the Middle East, and it just keeps getting bigger and bigger.
sentences.zh: 他们有两个绝密的中央情报局监听站。

sentences.en: They have two top-secret CIA listening posts.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到这种稳步加深的联系一直在发展。

sentences.en: So you're seeing this just steadily deepening ties developing all the time.
sentences.zh: 沙阿确实开始受到这些加深联系的鼓舞，向美国索取更多。

sentences.en: And the Shah really starts to feel emboldened by these deepening ties to ask for more and more from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他一直痴迷于建立一支世界级的军队，实际上从他统治之初，就一直指望美国在这方面提供帮助。

sentences.en: For years, he's been obsessed with building a world-class army, and really since the beginning of his reign, had looked to the United States for help in doing that.
sentences.zh: 1972年，美国第一次终于说，是的，你可以拥有它。

sentences.en: And for the first time in 1972, the United States finally said, yes, you could have it.
sentences.zh: 捍卫自由是每个人的事，不仅仅是美国的事。

sentences.en: The defense of freedom is everybody's business, not just America's business.
sentences.zh: 这之所以发生是因为一种叫做“尼克松主义”的东西。

sentences.en: And it happened because of something called the Nixon Doctrine.
sentences.zh: 但我们将指望直接受到威胁的国家承担起为其防御提供人力资源的主要责任。

sentences.en: But we shall look to the nation directly threatened to assume the primary responsibility of providing the manpower for its defense.
sentences.zh: 尼克松主义是任命对美国友好的地区大国作为该地区的警察。

sentences.en: The Nixon Doctrine is to appoint regional powers that are friendly to the United States as the policemen of the area.
sentences.zh: 在中东，有沙特阿拉伯和伊朗这两个支柱。

sentences.en: In the Middle East, there's the twin pillars of Saudi Arabia and Iran.
sentences.zh: 沙特阿拉伯更多是经济支柱，而伊朗将成为该地区的军事警察。

sentences.en: Saudi Arabia being much more of an economic one, Iran is going to become the military policemen of the region.
sentences.zh: 代表美国。

sentences.en: On behalf of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 代表美国。

sentences.en: On behalf of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切在尼克松1972年5月进行的那次广泛的国际访问中达到了顶点，其中包括在伊朗的停留。

sentences.en: So this all culminates in this extensive international trip Nixon took in May of 1972 that included a stopover in Iran.
sentences.zh: 对伊朗的访问是对华盛顿和德黑兰之间良好关系的肯定，特别是对伊朗沙阿和尼克松总统之间良好关系的肯定，他们相处得非常好。
